title: The Young Kaga Lady's Mystery Tour
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0969.txt, subs_resolved/0970.txt (701 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: actions are direct typed edges. case_type: attempted_murder (the case starts as a kidnapping-fraud/extortion but escalates to Rintaro Hagino assaulting Soichi Hayashi with a rock and then trying to kill his own accomplice Manabu Saikawa by locking him, bleeding, in a closet). Corrections vs. the old low-fidelity `cases/ep969-970_...json`: (1) the old file's culprit id (Hagino) was actually correct and is kept as `label.murderer_id` here -- no reversal needed; (2) the old file completely omitted Manabu Saikawa as a node, despite him being both the mastermind of the first staged kidnapping AND the near-victim of Hagino's attempted murder -- he is added here (person p6, roles suspect+victim); (3) the old file's single vague clue ("only Hagino had the trust/access") is replaced with the actual chain of physical evidence from the transcript: the photo showing Manabu's hands merely held behind his back (no rope burns) exposing his fake first kidnapping, the hikiko sawdust on the murder weapon narrowing suspects to the two printed-silk craftsmen, the three sets of footprints plus Manabu's disabled hand proving only Hagino could have swung the rock, and the smartphone-shaped bulge in Hagino's own "hostage" photo exposing his fake second kidnapping; (4) case_type corrected from the old file's plain "kidnapping" to "attempted_murder" since no one actually stays kidnapped by a third party -- both apparent kidnappings are frauds staged by the people later shown to be guilty, and the real crime is Hagino's assault on Soichi and attempted murder of Manabu. Takumi Kondo's storyline (accused over gold dust, confesses to an unrelated attempted theft of the ransom cash) is a genuine red herring, not padding invented for this rebuild.

clues.desc: Photo of 'restrained' Manabu shows his hands merely held behind his back in a reflection, with no rope burns -- proves he was never actually tied up.

Security footage of the disguised person who collected the first ransom bag shows their ears; ear shape is as individual as a fingerprint and can be matched to Manabu's own ears, exposing him as his own 'kidnapper'.
Photo of 'rescued' Rintaro shows a phone-shaped bulge in his pocket -- a genuine kidnapper would have confiscated a hostage's phone, so Rintaro was never really held.

Three sets of footprints at the assault scene (Soichi's, Manabu's, and one unidentified) plus the fact that the rock was too heavy to swing one-handed and Manabu can only use one hand -- proves only the third, unidentified person (Rintaro) could have struck Soichi.
Hikiko sawdust, used specifically by printed-silk craftsmen, found on the assault weapon -- narrows the attacker to Rintaro or Manabu, the only two yuzen craftsmen involved.
Airplane noise audible in the background of the second threatening ransom call points to a location near Komatsu Airport, the only airport near Kanazawa.
